texts.preamble: Pankaj Aggarwal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) on 18 March, 2021 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 8433/2016 Cc No. : 93/2006 U/S: : 16(1)(A) r/w Section 7 of P.F.A Act-1954 Pankaj Aggarwal, S/o Sh. Mahavir Prasad, M/s Aggarwal Sweet Opp. Shardanand College, Alipur, Delhi. .....Appellant versus The State ( Govt of Nct of Delhi), Service through Commissioner, Deptt of Prevention of Food Adulteration now office of the Commissioner of Food Safety ) A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 .....Respondent
texts.facts: The brief facts of the present case are that on 26.10.2005, at about 08:15p.m. the Food Inspectors Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta and Field Assistant Sh. Satish Kumar Gaur ; under the supervision of Local Health Authority/SDM Sh. Vijay Dogra, reached at the premises of appellant/accused M/s Aggarwal Sweets, Opposite Sharadhanand College, Alipur, Delhi, where appellant/accused Pankaj Aggarwal, vendor cum proprietor was found conducting business of various food articles which were lying stored/exposed for preparation of food article including Imli Ki Chatni for sale for human consumption ; - that FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of 'Imli Ki Chatni' from the vendor which was lying there in a Tin container bearing no label declaration ; - that thereafter as per the prescribed procedure under the PFA Act and Rules after giving notice to the vendor/appellant and offer towards the sale price of sample to which he agreed and accepted the sale consideration, sample was then lifted ; - that each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI in the presence of appellant/accused alongwith Panchnama etc was prepared at the spot ; the price of the sample commodity was paid to the vendor ; - that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 07.11.2005, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it was coloured with synthetic colouring matter with "Sunset Yellow FEF" ; that the sample was misbranded because of complete violation of Rule 32 of PFA Rules - that upon receipt of report, SDM/LHA directed investigation which was carried out by Food Inspection and after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 28.03.2006 alleging violation of Section 2(ia),(j) and (m) of PFA Act & Rules r/w Section 23,28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable under Section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act. - that the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with ; 4. The appellant/accused Pankaj Aggarwal being the Vendor cum Proprietor and Sh. Mahavir Prasad as Licencee of the said shop/business premises were summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 28.03.2006 for 08.04.2006 to face trial. Thereafter the accused persons appeared to face trial but during the trial proceedings Sh. Mahavir Prasad expired on 19.10.2007 and proceedings against him were abated vide order dated 18.11.2008. Pankaj Aggarwal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) on 18 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107673412/ 2 5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh.Suniti Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector. 6. On the basis of testimony of prosecution witnesses on 22.12.2009 charge was framed against the appellant/accused for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1A) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Sub clause 2(ia)(j)and(m) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 26.10.2005 at about 08.15 p.m, appellant/accused being the the Vendor cum Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Sweets sold for analysis approximately 1500 grams of "Imli Ki Chatni" taken from an open tin bearing no label declaration to Food Inspector Sh.Suniti Kumar Gupta on payment of sample commodity in the presence of LHA and witnesses and it was analyzed by the PA vide Certificate No. PFA/Enf./2590/2005 on 07.11.2005 and found that the sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring material viz sunset yellow FCF and violated the provisions of Section 2(ia)(a)(j) & (m) of PFA Act, 1954 and also violated the provision of Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, punishable under section 16(1A) of PFA Act, 1954 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of three witnesses of the department ( PW-1 Sh.Suniti Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector, PW-2 Sh.Satish Kumar Gaur, Field Assistant and PW-3 Sh. Vijay Dogra, Retired Jail Supdt, the then SDM/LHA prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused. 7. The statement of appellant/accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which he pleaded his innocence and stated that no efforts were made to join the public witnesses, the Imli Ki Chatni was lying in a plastic container ; that the container was not bearing label or declaration ; that the spoon used for taking sample was not dry and clean ; no payment was made as the commodity was not for sale ; consent was granted without application of mind, it is a false case and he has been falsely implicated. He prefer to lead defence evidence however, no witness was produced or examined as a defence witness. 9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds.
texts.arguments: Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. 10. During the course of argument on 18.03.2021, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 21.03.2014, and is confining his appeal limited to the quantum of sentence only awarded to him vide order dated 24.03.2014 ; and to affirm his submissions, appellant has tender his affidavit duly sworn and notarized by the Oath Commissioner, in that regard and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation as FSSAI. 11. Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to submission of appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency should be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food adulteration article / commodity leading to hazardous consequences on the health or body of a person. 12. I have carefully gone through the available record as well as trial court record, have heard the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties at length and have also gone through the judgments relied upon by the parties. 13. In light of above submissions and discussion particularly when the affidavit of appellant to this effect is filed on record, I find no valid and legal reasons to interfere with the well reasoned judgment of the learned trial court. II. Now Coming to the alternate plea of giving benefit of new legislation to the appellant/ accused. 14. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act has thereafter come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only. 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant is a man of 38 years of age, respectable person, has deep roots in the society and only sole bread earner of his family, the licencee of the M/s Aggarwal Sweets was his father, (accused no. 2 before the trial court ) has expired, and his mother is a paralytic patient, totally dependent upon him, is still running the same business at the same place, not involved into any offence under the PFA Act and there is no case subsequent thereto till date, and thus, prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of Pankaj Aggarwal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) on 18 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107673412/ 4 the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further it is stated that case pertains to the year 2006, the appellant/accused has faced the trial almost 15 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and, the hardships faced by him has caused him great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him. 15.2 In support of his submissions qua the consideration of the case under new legislation, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences have changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSAI have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". 15.5 That now in the FSSAI such adulteration is termed as "unsafe food" in terms of Section 3(zz)(viii) of FSSA Act and violation thereof is punishable u/s 59(1) of FSSA. - Sub-clause (viii) of 3(zz) FSSA Act is applicable where the colouring material or the preservative other than that specified in respect there of is found in the food article and not where the colouring material exceeds the prescribed limit. Pankaj Aggarwal vs The State ( Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) on 18 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107673412/ 5 15.8 Now, coming to the application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an offence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different. - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. 15-A - Academic Reference can also be made to the letter dated 03.10.2017 of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, produced before the court during the proceedings. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.
